cards.explanation: The answer is governor, friends. Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah over the people he left behind, and the commanders hear that Gedaliah has the job. A governor runs things for the king, and that's the seat Gedaliah sits in here.

The answer is Ishmael son of Nethaniah. He's on the list, right along with Johanan, Seraiah and Jaazaniah, and all four come to Gedaliah at Mizpah with their men. Keep his name handy, friends, because you'll hear it again in this passage.
The answer is the servants of the Chaldeans. Gedaliah says, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans.” He says it as an oath, before the commanders and their men.

The answer is that it will be well with them. Gedaliah says, “Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.” That's the whole promise, friends, plain and simple. He gives no timeline and adds no extras.

The answer is True, friends. The text says all the people, small and great, together with the commanders of the army, arose and fled to Egypt. Everybody is on the move at once. It's a heavy moment, and the passage doesn't soften it.

The answer is that they are afraid of the Chaldeans. The text says they fled to Egypt “…for fear of the Chaldeans.” The people small and great and the commanders of the army all arose and fled. Fear is the reason the verse names, friends, and it doesn't say anything beyond that.

The answer is that he releases him from prison, friends. Evil-merodach, the new king of Babylon, let King Jehoiachin out of prison in the year he became king. The text dates it to the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's exile. Prison door open, just like that.

The answer is False, friends. The text says the king spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon. Above, not below. I once got moved to the back of a junk drawer. Jehoiachin got moved UP.

The answer is False, friends. The text says Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and dined regularly at the king's table for the rest of his life. That's not a one-time honor. Prison clothes off, regular seat at the table. I'd have changed so fast my hat would've stayed behind.

The answer is for the rest of his life. The text says the king provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life. It's every single day, friends, with no end date written in. A good way to close out the passage.
